model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 total revenues $8,790M (rental and other $8,198M + strategic capital $592M; FY2025 supplemental, 8-K 0001193125-26-017256). The engine's 'ebitda_margin_path' is the HOUSE AFFO margin on this revenue line, not EBITDA. House AFFO = reported AFFO less the stock-compensation add-back (PLD's AFFO adds SBC back; the house basis does not), with realized development gains (net of current tax) carried at a NORMALISED level rather than as reported. FY2025: reported AFFO $4,335.0M - SBC $185.5M - development gains net $232.0M = $3,917.5M recurring (44.6% of revenue); + gains net $232.0M = $4,149.5M (47.2%). FY2026 year-1 margin 53.8% = ~47.0% recurring (H1-26 actual 49.0%, H2 is seasonally heavier in turnover capex and property improvements) + guided realized development gains $600-700M (~6.8% of ~$9.5B revenue).
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 weighted average diluted 957.884M = 933.092M basic common + 20.160M exchangeable limited-partnership units + 4.632M equity awards (Q2-2026 supplemental, 8-K 0001193125-26-305416). Core FFO and AFFO are stated attributable to common stockholders AND unitholders, so the divisor includes the OP units. Held FLAT: SBC is deducted in the house AFFO (not added back as PLD reports it), so diluting for it as well would double-count; diluted count has moved only 951.8M (FY2023) -> 957.9M (Q2-26), ~0.2%/yr. The pending SEGRO plc share issuance (0.0920 new PLD shares per SEGRO share, ~13% more shares before the cash alternative) is NOT included - the deal has not closed and its assets are not in the flows either.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO in the engine by design: AFFO is a post-interest flow capitalised at the cost of equity, so deducting net debt again would double-count it. Actual balance sheet at 30 June 2026 recorded in debt_memo.

debt_memo.source: Q2-2026 supplemental (8-K ex99.1, 0001193125-26-305416), Debt Components - Consolidated and press release balance-sheet section. Venture debt sits inside the unconsolidated-entity adjustments to AFFO, i.e. its interest is already in the flow.

inputs.fcf_definition: House AFFO FY2025 = PLD AFFO attributable to common stockholders/unitholders $4,335.0M less stock compensation amortization $185.5M (PLD adds it back; the house basis treats it as a cost). Realized development gains net of current tax ($257.7M - $25.7M = $232.0M) are INCLUDED: merchant development and contribution to the strategic-capital funds is a 20-year recurring activity at PLD and is guided every year. Already after interest, preferred dividends, straight-line rent and lease-intangible amortisation, property improvements and turnover costs (recurring capex), and the NCI/unconsolidated-venture adjustments. Development starts ($4.5-5.5B guided FY26) are growth capital funded by retained AFFO, capital recycling (contributions/dispositions $4.25-5.25B) and debt; they are what the growth path pays for and are not deducted again.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 supplemental AFFO reconciliation, 'Stock compensation amortization expense' $185.466M (equals XBRL ShareBasedCompensation in PLD_Metrics.csv). Deducted once by not adding it back to Core FFO. Equity-award withholding taxes ($23.9M FY25) are a financing-section item and are not deducted additionally - immaterial at 0.6% of AFFO.
inputs.buyback_note: No open-market repurchases in FY2025 or H1-2026; flat count rests on SBC being expensed, not on buybacks.
inputs.horizon_note: FY0 is FY2025 actual; year 1 is FY2026 (guided, H1 reported), years 2-10 are FY2027-FY2035. Valuation date is nine months into FY2026, so discounting the full FY2026 flow one year is mildly conservative.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC, because the capitalised flow is post-interest. USD build: 10-year US Treasury 5.24% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-10-01), equity risk premium 4.5%, beta ~0.9 (logistics REIT with 23.9% debt/total market cap, A-rated; Yahoo 5-year beta is inflated by the 2022 rate shock) -> 5.24 + 0.9 x 4.5 = 9.29%, rounded to 9.25%. Slightly above MAA (9.0%, beta 0.85) for PLD's development, data-centre and 20-country FX exposure. Cross-check: at the current price the stock trades on ~24x FY26E house AFFO (incl. normalised gains) and ~20.5x FY26E Core FFO; a 9.25% CoE with 3.0% terminal growth implies a 16.5x steady-state multiple, so the market is pricing either a lower discount rate (~8%) or a longer high-growth run than the base case. Single rate across scenarios; risk carried in the paths and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: PLD is the lessor. Ground-lease expense is inside rental expense and therefore inside AFFO.
inputs.nci_treatment: Exchangeable LP-unit NCI handled by valuing AFFO attributable to stockholders AND unitholders and dividing by shares + units. Consolidated co-investment-venture NCI is already stripped out by the 'adjustments related to noncontrolling interests' lines in PLD's AFFO reconciliation; PLD's share of unconsolidated ventures is added in the same reconciliation. Series Q preferred dividends (~$5.7M/yr) are deducted before net earnings attributable to common.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the Drivers/engine route with net debt held at zero (the MAA / GMG.AX / CHC.AX pattern). Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md 'REIT / property trust' row: PLD is a self-managed US REIT (logistics real estate plus a strategic-capital fund-management business and a merchant-development arm); GAAP net income carries ~$2.5B/yr of real-estate depreciation and lumpy disposition gains (FY24 $904M of non-development gains), and OCF-less-capex is not an owner-FCF series because development spend is growth capital. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). Engine components mapped as: revenue = total revenues (rental + strategic capital); ebitda_margin_path = house AFFO margin on revenue; SBC, D&A, capex, tax and working-capital paths = 0 (all already inside AFFO, or nil for a REIT). Core FFO / AFFO are non-GAAP and absent from XBRL; read from the FY2024 (0000950170-25-006999), FY2025 (0001193125-26-017256) and Q2-2026 (0001193125-26-305416) supplementals on EDGAR. Pre-FY2023 supplementals on EDGAR are image-only exhibits, so the AFFO series starts at FY2023. SEGRO plc acquisition (~$18.8B, all-share with partial cash alternative, expected close H1 2027) is deliberately NOT modelled: neither SEGRO's AFFO nor the ~124M new PLD shares are in the flows; it is a catalyst/risk to revisit at completion.

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_basis: House AFFO per diluted share+unit including realized development gains net of tax: FY2023 $4.67, FY2024 $4.39, FY2025 $4.34 (2-year CAGR -3.6%, the only span with text-extractable supplementals); excluding development gains FY2023 $4.22, FY2024 $3.99, FY2025 $4.09. Reported AFFO/share (with SBC added back): FY2023 $4.95, FY2024 $4.64, FY2025 $4.53. Core FFO/share: FY2023 $5.61 (incl. $0.51 net promote), FY2024 $5.56, FY2025 $5.81, FY2026E $6.26 (guidance midpoint $6.22-6.30, raised twice). Core FFO ex net promote: FY2023 $5.10, FY2024 $5.53, FY2025 ~$5.86, FY2026E $6.26 -> 7.1%/yr FY23-26E. Dividends + unit distributions: FY2023 $3,315M, FY2024 $3,667M, FY2025 $3,866M; Q2-26 run-rate $1,027M/qtr (~$4.29/share annualised).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Judgment: 10-year house AFFO/share CAGR of the base path from FY2025 actual ($4.33) to FY2035E. Not the equity CAGR: book equity is depreciated cost and the 5-year figure (+9.7%) is the October-2022 all-stock Duke Realty merger, while the 3-year figure (-0.1%) is depreciation plus a payout above GAAP earnings. Revenue CAGRs (13.8% / 14.6%) are also merger-inflated (Duke FY22, Liberty FY20).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-0.1% 3yr / +9.7% 5yr) diverges from revenue (+13.8% / +14.6%) and EPS (-5.8% / +12.1%) by well over 30%. Expected for a REIT that grew by two large all-stock mergers (Liberty Property Feb-2020, Duke Realty Oct-2022): per-share and book-equity series are discontinuous, GAAP equity shrinks with depreciation, and EPS swings with disposition gains. Growth selected from the AFFO/Core FFO per-share series instead.
historical_growth.notes: House AFFO/share fell FY2023 -> FY2025 while Core FFO ex promote rose ~7%/yr: the difference is the collapse of promote income after the FY2023 peak, lower development gains in FY2024-25 as cap rates widened, and rising turnover costs/property improvements. FY2026 turns it: H1-26 house AFFO ex gains $2,315M vs $1,986M in H1-25 (+16.6%), helped by lease mark-to-market (cash rent change +22.3% on Q2 rollovers) and positive promotes.

base.ebitda_margin_note: House AFFO margin on total revenue = recurring margin + normalised development gains. FY26 53.8% = ~47.0% recurring + guided $600-700M gains (6.8%). From FY27 gains normalise to ~4.5% of revenue (FY23 5.3%, FY24 4.7%, FY25 2.6%, FY26E 6.8%; average 4.85%). Recurring margin rises 47.5% -> 48.5% by FY2030 as the embedded lease mark-to-market rolls to cash NOI with little incremental cost, net of refinancing: $36.4B at a 3.3% average coupon rolling toward the 4.4% Q2-26 new-issue rate over a 7.9-year term (~$400M, ~3.5% of FY2030 revenue, absorbed over the horizon).
base.narrative: Revenue +8.0% FY26 (H1 +9.2%; cash same-store NOI guide +6.75-7.25%, plus development stabilisations and $1.5-2.0B acquisitions), then +7.0%/+6.5%/+6.0% FY27-29 as the remaining lease mark-to-market, ~$2.5B/yr of development stabilisations at ~6.3% yields and the first data-centre build-to-suits deliver, fading to 3.0% nominal by FY2035. House AFFO/share FY26E ~$5.33 -> FY35E ~$8.14. Terminal 3.0% at 9.25% cost of equity (~16.5x exit); the 20x cap does not bind.

bull.narrative: The broadening demand management describes (record 67 MSF leased in Q2-26, occupancy back to 95.5% and rising) meets a supply pipeline that shrank after 2023, so market rents re-accelerate and the mark-to-market stays wide; the 5.8 GW data-centre power pipeline converts into build-to-suits at 7%+ yields and contributions to funds keep development gains near $700M+/yr; promotes recover as fund values rise. Revenue compounds ~8-9% for four years, house AFFO margin reaches 55%, AFFO/share ~$9.6 by FY2035; terminal 3.5% (18x exit, 22x cap not binding).

bear.narrative: Higher-for-longer rates keep cap rates wide: development gains shrink to ~1.5% of revenue as contributions to funds slow and merchant margins compress (as in FY2025, $232M), promotes stay near zero, and the 3.3%-coupon debt stack reprices toward 5%+. Tariff-driven trade disruption and the 2026 development surge ($4.5-5.5B PLD starts alone) soften market rents so the mark-to-market is exhausted by 2028; revenue grows ~3% after FY26. House AFFO margin falls to 46.5% and AFFO/share is ~$5.9 by FY2035; terminal 2.5% with a 16x cap (Gordon at 9.25%/2.5% is ~15.2x, so Gordon binds).

scenario_narratives.base: Embedded rent growth carries FY26-FY28: cash same-store NOI +7% this year, Q2-26 cash rent change on rollover still +22%, and ~$2.5B/yr of development stabilising at ~6.3% yields. Development gains normalise to ~4.5% of revenue and refinancing from a 3.3% average coupon absorbs part of the operating upside. House AFFO/share compounds ~6.5%/yr for a decade, then a 3% perpetuity at a 9.25% cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bull: Logistics demand broadens while new supply stays below the 2022-23 peak, the data-centre power bank (5.8 GW) monetises through build-to-suits and fund contributions, and development gains and promotes run at or above the FY26 guide. AFFO/share compounds ~8%/yr and the business earns a 3.5% terminal growth rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: Rates stay above 5% on the 10-year, cap rates widen, development and promote income dry up, and refinancing plus a softer leasing market (tariffs, a supply bulge from the current development wave) hold revenue growth to ~3%. AFFO/share grows only ~2.5%/yr; the balance sheet (4.7x debt/EBITDA, 7.9-year term, 23.9% debt/market cap) keeps this an earnings problem, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Close to the 15/50/35 house default. Bear lifted to 20% because the dominant variables - long rates, cap rates and therefore development gains and promotes - are macro and outside PLD's control, and the pending SEGRO deal adds integration and dilution risk the flows do not carry. Bull held at 30% (not 35%) because it needs data-centre monetisation at scale, which management itself says is constrained by power and local opposition. Not more bear: guidance has been raised twice in 2026, occupancy and leasing are at records, and leverage is modest for a REIT.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Prologis is valued on the cash it can distribute - AFFO after interest, recurring capex, straight-line rent and stock compensation, plus a normalised level of realized development gains - capitalised at a 9.25% USD cost of equity off a 5.24% 10-year Treasury, with net debt NOT deducted a second time. Three explicit ten-year AFFO paths bracket the mark-to-market runway, the development/data-centre opportunity and the refinancing headwind. GAAP EPS, P/E, EV/EBITDA and book equity are not used: depreciation, disposition gains and two all-stock mergers make them uninformative. The pending SEGRO acquisition is not modelled.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: each 50bp on the 9.25% rate moves base value roughly 8-10%; the 5.24% 10-year Treasury used is high by post-2009 standards and the valuation rises if rates mean-revert

Development gains and promotes: ~6.8% of FY26 revenue from realized development gains is cap-rate dependent; the base normalises it to 4.5% and the bear to 1.5% - the single largest margin swing between scenarios
Refinancing: $36.4B of debt at a 3.3% average coupon (7.9-year term) reprices toward the 4.4% Q2-26 new-issue rate or higher; each 100bp on the full stack is ~$360M, ~7% of FY26 house AFFO

SEGRO plc (~$18.8B, 0.0920 PLD shares per SEGRO share plus partial cash, close expected H1 2027): unmodelled; adds ~13% to the share count before the cash alternative and brings a lower-growth UK/European portfolio, so per-share accretion is the question to revisit at completion
Data-centre pivot: the 5.8 GW power pipeline and ~$25B ambition are unproven at PLD's scale; power, permitting and community opposition could delay the bull case
Leadership change: Dan Letter became CEO 1 January 2026 with Hamid Moghadam as Executive Chairman; capital allocation through the SEGRO integration is the first big test

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 111.03-153.35
data_sources.financials: SEC EDGAR 8-K earnings supplementals (ex99.1): Q2-2026 (0001193125-26-305416) for H1-26 Core FFO/AFFO reconciliation, diluted shares+units, debt and liquidity, FY2026 guidance; FY2025 (0001193125-26-017256) and FY2024 (0000950170-25-006999) for full-year Core FFO, AFFO, SBC and development gains FY2023-FY2025. SEC XBRL companyfacts as carried in PLD_Metrics.csv for revenue, net income, EPS, equity and SBC history.
